subject.title: macOS: Gateway daemon PATH excludes user bin dirs (nix, bun, local, etc.)

question: Should macOS Gateway LaunchAgents keep the canonical system-only service PATH, add an explicit operator opt-in for user bin directories, or include user bin directories by default?
rationale: Current source, docs, and tests intentionally harden macOS LaunchAgent PATHs, while the requested behavior improves Nix/Bun/local tool discovery and changes command-resolution trust; automation should not choose that tradeoff.

options.title: Keep default minimal, add explicit opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current safe default and add a documented, tested operator-controlled service PATH opt-in if maintainers want to support this workflow.

options.title: Change the macOS default
options.body: Include Darwin user-bin directories by default and require fresh-install, reinstall, upgrade, and command-resolution security proof before landing.

options.title: Decline service PATH expansion
options.body: Leave daemon PATH policy unchanged and direct users to exec PATH controls, login-shell PATH behavior, or standard system install locations.

recommendation.title: Keep default minimal, add explicit opt-in
recommendation.body: Preserve the current safe default and add a documented, tested operator-controlled service PATH opt-in if maintainers want to support this workflow.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the clearest current policy owner signal from the adjacent managed service PATH precedence decision on the merged pnpm PATH PR.
